findings.message: T001 is attributed to `ExplicitTrackBranch`, `TrackBranchClaim`, and `BranchReaderPort`, but the task text explicitly says those reference-only entries are unchanged. Remove those attributions or the contract no longer matches the described edit scope.

T005 is attributed to `FileArgs`, `CommitFromFileArgs`, and `UnstageArgs`, but the task text says the `AddAll` / `AddFromFile` / `CommitFromFile` / `NoteFromFile` / `Unstage` variants keep their existing shape and tests. Those symbol attributions look inflated for the described change.

The `plan.summary` block is prose-heavy restatement of the upstream ADR/spec behavior (`bin/sotp git sync` semantics, hexagonal layering, D7/D8 rationale) instead of an executable plan. The impl-plan review policy only permits target + operation + anchor cite here, so this section should be collapsed into taskable edits rather than restating the design contract.

`T005` is attributed to `FileArgs`, `CommitFromFileArgs`, and `UnstageArgs`, but the task text only removes `SwitchAndPull`, adds `Sync`, and rewires the git-family dispatch path; it explicitly says the `AddAll` / `AddFromFile` / `CommitFromFile` / `NoteFromFile` / `Unstage` variants keep their existing shape. Those three catalog entries are therefore over-attributed and make the task-contract imply a broader edit than the plan actually describes.

S1-S7 (and the task bullets beneath them) restate upstream ADR/spec behavior in prose instead of staying in the executable-plan format. Examples include 'exact stdout/stderr/exit contracts', 'git pull --ff-only classified into 3 typed SyncError variants', and 'graceful skip forbidden'. The impl-plan prompt only allows target + operation + anchor cite, so this text needs to be collapsed into action items.

T002 over-attributes `BranchReaderPort` even though the task text explicitly says 'Reference-only entries (ExplicitTrackBranch, TrackBranchClaim, BranchReaderPort) are unchanged'. That catalogue entry is not part of the work and should be removed from the task-contract map.

AC-03 is mapped only to T005, but T006 explicitly owns deletion of `apps/cli-composition/src/git.rs` helpers `git_switch_and_pull_in` / `git_switch_and_pull_impl` in `impl-plan.json` line 36. AC-03 requires those symbols to be absent, so the load-bearing coverage is split incorrectly: T005 could be treated as covering AC-03 while the helper deletion is deferred to an unmapped task. Add T006 to AC-03 coverage or move that deletion fully into T005.

T009 includes `Add switch-and-pull grep assertion` without naming the target file, script, task, or symbol where that assertion should be added. The rest of T009 names files, but this persistent verification step lacks a target boundary, so an executor has to invent where it belongs.

AC-10/IN-11 require replacing the non-test `apps/cli/src/commands/track/branch_ops.rs` git判定/direct infrastructure path, but the plan never assigns that production edit. `task-coverage.json` maps AC-10 to T005/T006/T008, while T005 only covers `apps/cli/src/commands/git.rs`, T006 covers `apps/cli-composition`, and T008 mentions only `branch_ops.rs tests` cleanup. An implementer can follow all tasks and still leave the production `branch_ops.rs` rev-parse/GitRepository path outside the plan.

AC-09 is only mapped to T003, but T003 just adds the interactor types and mock-port tests; it does not migrate the live track/pr/review_v2 composition flows that AC-09 requires to be orchestrated through those interactors. The executable tasks that perform that migration are T006/T007, and T007 even cites AC-09 in impl-plan.json, so leaving AC-09 covered solely by T003 makes the coverage map report the acceptance criterion complete before the actual caller migration is covered.

P1 task-contract attribution mismatch: `T001`, `T002`, and `T004` still describe modifying `GitWorkflowError`, `GitPrimitivePort`, and `SyncError`, but those catalogue entries were removed from `task-contract.json` and moved elsewhere. The contract no longer matches the executable plan for those tasks.

P1 upstream restatement: `T010`/`T011` and the mirrored `S8` prose in `plan.md` spell out upstream rationale/behavior (`process-spawn failure is an infra-availability failure`, `composition = wiring only`, `bit-for-bit`) instead of staying at `target + operation + anchor cite`, which violates `knowledge/conventions/no-upstream-restatement.md`.

T001 still says it will retype `GitWorkflowError` variants, but the contract block for T001 only attributes `DiagnosticText` plus the validator helpers. Restore `GitWorkflowError` attribution here or remove that work from the task description.

T002 declares `GitPrimitivePort` as part of the task, but the contract block for T002 only attributes `TrackArchiveFsPort` and related value types. That leaves the port itself unowned in task-contract.
T004 declares `SyncError` variants and sync tests, but the contract block for T004 omits `SyncError` entirely. This under-attributes the task relative to the executable plan text.

T004: `impl-plan.json` / `plan.md` says `libs/infrastructure/src/git_cli/workflow_adapter.rs` will add `FsGitWorkflowAdapter` primitive-method implementations, and `libs/infrastructure/src/git_cli/mod.rs` will add `SystemGitRepo::sync_current_branch`, but the T004 block in `task-contract.json` only attributes `SyncError` and `FsWorkspaceAdapter`. The modified `FsGitWorkflowAdapter` and `SystemGitRepo` catalogue entries are omitted, so the task/contract pair is inconsistent.

T010: the task text updates `libs/infrastructure/src/git_cli/workflow_adapter.rs` error mapping, which means `FsGitWorkflowAdapter` is being modified, but the T010 block in `task-contract.json` only attributes `GitWorkflowError`, `SyncError`, and `persist_commit_hash_for_track`. `FsGitWorkflowAdapter` is missing from the attribution set.

T011: the task text implements `resolve_repo_root` on `libs/infrastructure/src/git_cli/workflow_adapter.rs`, so `FsGitWorkflowAdapter` is part of the change, but the T011 block in `task-contract.json` never attributes that adapter. The contract is under-specified for this task.

T010 is under-attributed in `task-contract.json`: the task text in `impl-plan.json:60` explicitly edits `apps/cli-composition/src/track/branch_strategy.rs` (`switch_base_error_to_outcome`), but the T010 contract only lists usecase/infrastructure entries plus `persist_commit_hash_for_track`. The corresponding `cli_composition` entry is missing, so the contract does not cover the full task surface.

T011 is under-attributed in `task-contract.json`: the task text in `impl-plan.json:66` explicitly edits `apps/cli-composition/src/telemetry.rs` to replace `TelemetryAggregateServiceImpl` wiring, but the T011 contract only names usecase/infrastructure entries. No `cli_composition` entry is attributed for the composition-layer rewrite, so the task-contract mapping is incomplete.

`T010` attributes `cli_composition::GitCompositionRoot`, but the T010 task description only touches `libs/usecase/src/git_workflow.rs`, `libs/infrastructure/src/git_cli/{workflow_adapter,mod}.rs`, `apps/cli-composition/src/track/branch_strategy.rs`, and `apps/cli-composition/src/review_v2/commit_hash.rs`. It does not modify `apps/cli-composition/src/git.rs` or the `GitCompositionRoot` catalogue entry, so this task-contract attribution is not supported by the task.

`T011` attributes `cli_composition::GitCompositionRoot`, but its task description is for `GitPrimitivePort::resolve_repo_root`, telemetry usecase/interactor additions, `FsArchivedTelemetryFactoryAdapter`, and `apps/cli-composition/src/telemetry.rs` wiring. It does not touch `apps/cli-composition/src/git.rs::GitCompositionRoot`; the attribution should match the telemetry composition surface actually described by T011.

T001/T002/T004 still retain task-contract ownership for entries that S8 later changes into their final shape: `GitWorkflowError` is still attributed to T001 while T010 adds `SwitchFailed`, `GitPrimitivePort` is still attributed to T002 while T011 adds `resolve_repo_root`, and `SyncError` is still attributed to T004 while T010 adds `Spawn` and extracts classification. That defeats the deferred/final-Blue attribution model for these catalogue entries and can let intermediate tasks claim coverage before the later repayment tasks complete the actual final surface.

T011's contract attributes distinct catalogue entries `TelemetryReportInteractor` and `TelemetryEmitInteractor`, but the T011 executable description only says to add `ArchivedTelemetryFactoryPort`, `TelemetryAggregateInteractor::new / report / emit_archived`, `FsArchivedTelemetryFactoryAdapter`, and composition wiring. There is no target+operation for adding or modifying those two interactor entries, so the task-contract claims catalogue work that the task description does not actually touch.

`tasks[].description` for `T004` restates upstream behavior contract instead of staying in target + operation + anchor form: `typed failure classification for the 3 fail-closed modes (upstream-not-set / non-fast-forward / worktree-unresolved)`. Per `knowledge/conventions/no-upstream-restatement.md`, remove the prose and keep only the file/symbol change plus the anchor cite.

`tasks[].description` for `T011` restates upstream design rationale instead of staying in target + operation + anchor form: `reshape TelemetryAggregateInteractor into a facade over both sub-interactors (validation locus + delegation)`. Per `knowledge/conventions/no-upstream-restatement.md`, trim the rationale prose and keep only the change target, the operation, and the anchor cite.

T010 is under-attributed in `task-contract.json`: the task text at `impl-plan.json:60` edits `libs/infrastructure/src/git_cli/workflow_adapter.rs` and `apps/cli-composition/src/track/branch_strategy.rs`, but the contract only names `GitWorkflowError`, `SyncError`, and `persist_commit_hash_for_track`. The touched `FsGitWorkflowAdapter` / composition-layer branch-switch surface is not represented, so the task-contract mapping is incomplete.

T011 is under-attributed in `task-contract.json`: the task text at `impl-plan.json:66` explicitly edits `apps/cli-composition/src/telemetry.rs` to replace `TelemetryAggregateServiceImpl` wiring, but the contract only names usecase/infrastructure entries. No `cli_composition` telemetry/wiring entry is attributed for that composition-layer rewrite, so the task-contract mapping is incomplete.

T010 attributes the `FsGitWorkflowAdapter` catalogue entry even though this track's final-Blue-state attribution model makes that entry T011-exclusive; T010's workflow_adapter work is only an intermediate error-mapping change and T011 already owns the final adapter state. Keeping both attributions creates duplicate ownership and undermines the task-contract signal, so remove the T010 `FsGitWorkflowAdapter` entry and keep the T011 attribution.

T011 is mapped to `IN-10` / `CN-03` / `AC-09`, but the task text only adds usecase/infrastructure telemetry pieces and says to verify wiring; it never names a composition-root telemetry file or an operation to rewire it. Because AC-09 requires the composition root to become wiring-only for archived-track telemetry emit, an executor could complete this task without moving the composition implementation. Add an explicit target and operation for the apps/cli-composition telemetry wiring update.

GO-02/IN-07 explicitly include `cli_driver` in the layers whose git command strings and failure-detection logic must be moved behind infrastructure semantics, but the acceptance checks here only grep `apps/cli` and `apps/cli-composition`. AC-06 proves `apps/cli` dispatches through `GitDriver`, but it does not deterministically assert that `apps/cli-driver` itself contains no direct git command literals or failure classification, so the `cli_driver` portion of the stated goal can pass unverified.
findings.category: missing AC coverage for a stated goal

findings.message: `fs::read_dir(path)` will follow a symlinked `path` and enumerate the target directory, but this port method never performs the explicit `symlink_metadata()`/reject check used elsewhere in the infrastructure boundary. That lets an untrusted caller hand in a symlink and read entries outside the intended workspace tree.

The new `TrackArchiveFsPort` implementation uses raw `std::fs::create_dir_all` / `fs::rename` after only checking the queried path itself, so a symlinked ancestor under `track/` or `archive/` can redirect archive operations outside the trusted repo root. `path_is_dir` / `path_exists` also only inspect the leaf via `symlink_metadata`, so they do not close that boundary.

This classifier folds `Command::output()` spawn failures into `SyncError::WorktreeUnresolved`, so a missing/broken git binary or permission failure is reported as a dirty-worktree sync problem instead of an infrastructure failure. The new stderr matcher is also brittle and has no regression coverage for the non-fast-forward / worktree branches.

`move_path` accepts any path that does not strip the repo prefix by falling back to the original `src`/`dst` values. That means absolute paths outside the repo, and `..`-based paths that fail prefix stripping, are forwarded to `git mv` instead of being rejected, which bypasses the trusted-root boundary for this filesystem-mutating adapter.

`classify_sync_failure` falls through to `SyncError::WorktreeUnresolved` for every `git pull --ff-only` failure that does not match the two string checks. That downgrades unrelated git errors such as auth/network/remote corruption, and future wording changes in git, into the same non-fatal path as a dirty worktree, so callers can report success after a real sync failure. Unknown stderr should not be swallowed into the warning path.

`switch_to_base` downgrades `SyncNonFastForward` and `SyncWorktreeUnresolved` to a warning and then returns `Ok(...)`, so `git sync` can report success even though `git pull --ff-only` failed. The surrounding docs say only `SyncUpstreamNotSet` is the non-fatal case; the other sync failures should propagate so callers do not continue on a stale branch.

`commit_from_file` wraps pure branch-guard failures from `verify_explicit_track_branch` / `verify_auto_detected_branch` in `GitWorkflowError::Unavailable`, which turns a user-context or validation failure into an infrastructure outage. Callers can no longer distinguish a branch mismatch or missing claim from a real git/process failure, so the abstraction boundary is lost.

`switch_to_base` now folds `SyncNonFastForward` into the warning/`Ok(String)` path, but this test still calls `unwrap_err()` and expects that variant to propagate. As written, the usecase test suite fails before it can validate the new orchestration contract; update this case to assert the warning output or restore propagation in the implementation.

`current_branch_track_id` collapses every parse error except `InvalidTrackId` into `Ok(None)`, so `DetachedHead` and `NoBranch` are treated as "no track" instead of a failure. In the `CurrentBranchTrackIdStrict` CLI path that becomes a successful exit, which silently hides detached-HEAD / branch-detection problems.

If the `logs/` rename fails, the attempted rollback `self.git.move_path(Some(project_root), &dst_dir, &src_dir)` discards its result. A second failure can leave the track half-archived while the API only reports the original rename error, so the caller cannot tell the rollback also failed.

`TelemetryAggregateInteractor::emit_archived` builds `telemetry_dir` from a raw `track_id` string without validating it as a `domain::TrackId`. A malformed id such as `../evil` would escape `track/archive` and let the archived telemetry writer write outside the intended tree if a caller bypasses the CLI-level prevalidation.

The new public `GitWorkflowInteractor` APIs are missing direct coverage for their success/forwarding paths: `current_branch_track_id` only has detached-head/no-branch tests, and `sync_current_branch` is only exercised indirectly through `switch_to_base`. A regression in branch parsing or sync delegation could ship without a failing test.

`TelemetryAggregateInteractor::emit_archived` has no test that `ArchivedTrackTelemetryPort::emit` failures are propagated as `EmitUnavailable`; the current tests only cover the happy path, repo-root failure, and malformed `items_dir`.

`archive_track` records that `logs/` existed before the `git mv`, but this branch only handles the case where `dst_logs` is absent and `src_logs` is still present. If the git move or adapter behavior leaves neither path present, the function falls through to `Ok(...)`, reporting a successful archive after losing the archived telemetry logs. This should fail closed and roll back when `logs_was_dir` is true and `dst_logs` is not present.

On a filesystem rename failure, the rollback attempts `git mv dst_dir src_dir` while `src_dir` still exists because it contains the untracked `logs/` directory. The real git adapter will reject moving the archive directory over an existing source directory, so the rollback path leaves tracked files under `track/archive/...` and logs under `track/items/...`. The previous composition logic moved archive children back into the existing source directory before removing the empty archive dir; this interactor should preserve that behavior through the existing fs port methods.

P1: `execute_branch_create`/`execute_branch_switch` still perform domain validation and branch-name derivation in the CLI layer before dispatching to `TrackDriver` (`validate_track_id_str`, `format!("track/{track_id}")`, `validate_track_branch_str`, and `resolve_project_root`). Under the cli thin-bin policy, ADR D5/D8 require these handlers to only parse args, build `TrackInput`, call `TrackCompositionRoot::new().track_driver().handle(...)`, and emit the `CommandOutcome`; this pre-dispatch business logic should move behind the driver/usecase boundary. The same pattern is repeated in the switch path around line 64.

D5-D9 split the new sync refactor across three ownership layers without choosing one coherent public contract. D5 introduces `sync_current_branch`/`SyncError` at the infrastructure boundary, D6 rehomes sync/pull separation into the `GitWorkflowService` port chain, and D8/D9 then move orchestration out of composition root and cli. As written, `spec.json` and the later type catalogue cannot derive a single API surface or error-mapping boundary for `git sync`, so implementers can satisfy the prose while wiring incompatible layers.
findings.category: inconsistent decisions within the same ADR

findings.message: Several `docs` fields in the new/modified catalog entries restate ADR/spec rationale instead of staying anchor-only, which violates `knowledge/conventions/no-upstream-restatement.md`. The clearest instance is `usecase::git_workflow::DiagnosticText` at line 38, and the same pattern recurs in `GitWorkflowError`, `GitWorkflowInteractor`, `GitPrimitivePort`, `TrackArchiveFsPort`, `GitWorkflowService`, and the corresponding CLI/infrastructure entries: they explain why the design exists rather than just naming the changed surface and citing the anchors.

`contract-map.md` still renders `FsGitWorkflowAdapter` as implementing `GitWorkflowService`, but the catalogue declares that trait impl as `action: delete` and the replacement `GitPrimitivePort` impl as `action: add`. Because deleted `SwitchAndPullArgs` / `GitRepository` nodes are omitted from the map, this stale live edge makes the rendered type contract contradict the target-state catalogue and preserves the old adapter-to-application-service relationship in the PR-level view.

The `docs` field for `usecase::git_workflow::GitPrimitivePort` is restating the upstream contract in prose (per-method git semantics, explicit implementation target, and branch-root behavior) instead of staying at the required "change + operation + anchor cite" level. This violates `knowledge/conventions/no-upstream-restatement.md`; the same pattern also appears in `cli::commands::git::GitCommand`, `cli_driver::git::GitInput`, and `cli_composition::git::GitCompositionRoot`.

`GitWorkflowService::current_branch_track_id` still returns `Result<Option<String>, GitWorkflowError>` here, so the service boundary exports a branch-derived track identifier as a raw string instead of a validated domain type. That keeps the track-id contract stringly typed and pushes re-validation onto every caller.

`domain-types.json` is missing the reference nodes needed by this track's usecase surface: `BranchReadError` (`usecase-types.json:555`), `domain::TrackId` (`:644`, `:656`, `:678`, `:702`, `:732`) and `domain::CommitHash` (`:302`, `:712`, `:733`, `:741`). Without those declarations, the contract map leaves the new cross-layer type edges unresolved.

`TrackGitInteractor` method docs restate upstream behavior contracts instead of only citing anchors: the catalogue spells out the branch-create sequence, switch-base sequence, archive rollback sequence, and stdout behavior. `knowledge/conventions/no-upstream-restatement.md` applies to `<layer>-types.json` docs/intent fields, so this creates a second behavioral source of truth that can drift from IN-05/IN-10/CN-03/AC-04. Replace the prose with target/operation plus anchor cites.

The PR/review interactor method docs also encode behavior flow details (`fetch_branch -> show_file_at_ref(...) -> raw JSON` and current-branch verification before resolving HEAD) rather than deferring to the cited spec anchors. This violates the same no-upstream-restatement rule for type catalogues and makes these usecase entries independent behavioral documentation instead of type contracts tied to IN-10/CN-03/AC-09.

The catalogue adds `ArchivedTelemetryFactoryPort::build` returning `std::sync::Arc<dyn ArchivedTrackTelemetryPort>` in `usecase-types.json`, but the rendered `contract-map.md` never draws that dependency edge. The telemetry subgraph therefore no longer matches the type catalogue and hides the new factory return type.

`GitWorkflowError` docs cite `CN-05` and `AC-04`, but the structured `spec_refs` omit both. Catalogue traceability is driven by `spec_refs`, not prose, so the switch-base / bit-equivalence grounding for the new `SwitchFailed` contract is invisible to catalogue-spec verification and can drift. Add those anchors to `spec_refs`, or remove them from the docs if they are not actually part of this entry's contract.

`TelemetryAggregateInteractor` is declared as one interactor holding `GitPrimitivePort`, `TelemetryReportPort`, and `ArchivedTelemetryFactoryPort`, which bundles report aggregation with archived telemetry emit/repo-root orchestration. Those query and command concerns change for different reasons, and the report path now depends on git plus archive-emitter factory wiring it does not need. Split report and emit into separate interactors/services, or explicitly catalogue a thin facade over separate usecase ports if a single driver-facing facade is required.

`TelemetryReportInteractor`'s `docs` field restates the design rationale for the SRP split and dependency shape (`report path only`, split so it carries no git/factory dependency) instead of limiting the catalogue entry to target + operation + anchor cites. `knowledge/conventions/no-upstream-restatement.md` requires type-catalogue docs to reference upstream behavior by anchor, not reproduce the rationale in prose.

`TelemetryEmitInteractor`'s `docs` field restates the archived telemetry emit orchestration sequence (`repo-root resolution via GitPrimitivePort::resolve_repo_root`, then factory-built `ArchivedTrackTelemetryPort`). That is IN-10/CN-03 behavior prose in the downstream type catalogue; per `knowledge/conventions/no-upstream-restatement.md`, keep this as changed type + operation + anchors.

`TelemetryAggregateInteractor`'s `docs` field restates the facade/delegation design and relocation rationale for the telemetry service (`delegating report -> ...`, `emit_archived -> ...`, SRP split, relocated from cli_composition). This reproduces upstream design rationale in the catalogue instead of citing IN-10/CN-03/AC-09 only, violating `knowledge/conventions/no-upstream-restatement.md`.

`SyncError`'s `docs` field restates the upstream sync failure contract and mapping behavior (`3 fail-closed sync modes`, `Sync modes map 1:1...`, `Spawn maps...`) instead of limiting the catalogue entry to the changed type surface plus anchor cites. Per `knowledge/conventions/no-upstream-restatement.md`, downstream type catalogue docs must not reproduce IN-06/CN-02/AC-08 behavior in prose because that creates a second source of truth.

`TelemetryEmitInteractor::emit_archived`'s method `docs` restate the orchestration behavior (`Emits an archived-track telemetry event; resolves the repo root via GitPrimitivePort::resolve_repo_root`) while also citing IN-10/CN-03/AC-09. The type catalogue should identify the method and cite the anchors, not duplicate the upstream behavior contract in prose.

`TelemetryReportInteractor::report` and `TelemetryEmitInteractor::emit_archived` are added usecase-facing contracts but both accept `track_id` as raw `&str`. Other added git interactors in this same catalogue use `&domain::TrackId` for track identifiers, and the briefing explicitly calls out using `domain::TrackId` instead of raw strings where appropriate. Keeping these telemetry contracts stringly makes invalid track IDs representable at the usecase boundary; the methods should take a validated `domain::TrackId` or validate before exposing the downstream port contract.

Several updated `docs` fields restate downstream behavior/contract instead of staying at `change target + operation + anchor cite`, which violates `knowledge/conventions/no-upstream-restatement.md`: `TelemetryAggregateInteractor` here, plus the same pattern in `/home/flip451/individual/t-rust/templates/SoTOHE-core-003/track/items/remote-sync-dedicated-command-2026-07-04/infrastructure-types.json:70` (`SystemGitRepo`), `.../infrastructure-types.json:127` (`FsArchivedTelemetryFactoryAdapter`), and `.../cli_composition-types.json:63` (`persist_commit_hash_for_track`).

Several updated `docs` fields restate the contract/wiring instead of pointing at the upstream anchors, which violates the no-upstream-restatement rule and creates a second source of truth for the type contract: `/home/flip451/individual/t-rust/templates/SoTOHE-core-003/track/items/remote-sync-dedicated-command-2026-07-04/usecase-types.json` (`TelemetryAggregateInteractor` at line 259 and `ArchivedTelemetryFactoryPort` at line 316), `/home/flip451/individual/t-rust/templates/SoTOHE-core-003/track/items/remote-sync-dedicated-command-2026-07-04/infrastructure-types.json` (`SystemGitRepo` at line 61 and `FsArchivedTelemetryFactoryAdapter` at line 118), and `/home/flip451/individual/t-rust/templates/SoTOHE-core-003/track/items/remote-sync-dedicated-command-2026-07-04/cli_composition-types.json` (`persist_commit_hash_for_track` at line 55). These fields should be reduced to a terse type summary plus anchor cites.

`persist_commit_hash_for_track` is still a `pub fn` with the stringly-typed return type `Result<String, String>`. This layer is supposed to use typed composition errors so callers can handle failures structurally, not by parsing strings.

The exported validators in this module still return `Result<(), String>` (`validate_track_id_str` and `validate_review_group_name_str`). Public CLI-composition entry points should return a typed error enum instead of leaking stringly failures.

`TelemetryAggregateServiceImpl` is a secondary adapter implementation defined inside `cli_composition` and it implements `usecase::TelemetryAggregateService` here. That violates the layer boundary this scope is reviewing; the implementation belongs in `infrastructure`, with `cli_composition` only wiring it.

`signal_check_gate` defines `AdrChainAdapter`, `SpecAdrChainAdapter`, and `LayerChainAdapter` locally and implements `AdrChainRunnerPort` / `SpecAdrChainRunnerPort` / `LayerChainRunnerPort` inside `cli_composition`. These are secondary adapter implementations in the composition layer instead of infrastructure.

Delegating `track_archive` to `TrackGitInteractor::archive_track` removed the previous rollback-on-log-rename-failure behavior. If `git mv` succeeds and the follow-up `logs/` rename fails, the command now returns an error after leaving the track partially moved under `track/archive`, which is a data-loss regression.

`track_switch_base` no longer preserves the old contract of treating every non-zero `git pull --ff-only` result as a warning. `TrackGitInteractor::switch_to_base` now surfaces `SyncNonFastForward` and `SyncWorktreeUnresolved` as errors, so this path can fail where the previous composition returned exit 0 with a warning, breaking the bit-equivalent CLI behavior called out in the brief.

The old implementation forced `+refs/heads/<branch>:refs/remotes/origin/<branch>` before reading `origin/<branch>:track/items/.../metadata.json`; the new plain `fetch origin <branch>` path depends on the clone's default fetch refspec. On a single-branch or custom-refspec clone, `origin/<branch>` may not be refreshed, so omitted `--method` resolution can read stale track metadata.

`track_switch_base` no longer preserves the legacy checkout-failure outcome. The old `git_switch_and_pull_impl` returned `Ok(CommandOutcome { stdout: Some("Failed to checkout {branch}"), exit_code: git_code })` when checkout failed, so the CLI printed that stdout and returned git's status. The new wiring delegates to `TrackGitInteractor::switch_to_base`, whose first `switch_branch` failure is propagated as `Err` here and then rendered by `outcome_to_exit` as stderr with a generic failure exit. That breaks the briefing's CN-05 bit-equivalence requirement for `track_switch_base` on the switch/checkout failure path.

`switch_base_error_to_outcome` assembles user-facing command output in the composition layer via `stdout: Some(format!("Failed to checkout {base_branch}"))`. Under the cli_composition policy, rendering/output templating belongs in `cli_driver` (ADR D2/D3); this fallback should return typed state/error data and let the driver render the legacy message.

`pr_wait_and_merge` constructs `FsGitWorkflowAdapter` and invokes `GitPrimitivePort::fetch_branch` directly from cli_composition. That leaves a git side effect in the composition root instead of routing through the PR git interactor/driver boundary; the following metadata helper already goes through `PrGitInteractor::fetch_and_read_metadata_at_ref`, so this fetch should not be performed here. This is an invoke/wiring leak under the cli_composition policy and ADR D2.

`persist_commit_hash_for_track` constructs `FsGitWorkflowAdapter` and calls `GitPrimitivePort::resolve_commit` directly to resolve `HEAD`. That keeps the `git rev-parse HEAD` operation in cli_composition rather than routing it through the review git interactor boundary, violating the T007 routing intent and the wiring-only rule for the composition root.

`.harness/workflows/track/done.md:26-33` makes the sync step warning-only for `UpstreamNotSet` / `NonFastForward` / `WorktreeUnresolved`, but the same workflow still says the output should confirm the tree is 'updated from origin' and `.claude/commands/track/done.md:19-21` asks for it to be 'up to date with origin'. That lets `/track:done` report a successful completion even when the ff-only pull failed, so the completion contract is false in the warning path. Reword the summary/output to say the sync was attempted unless the pull actually succeeded.

P1: The new `done` workflow docs overstate the sync failure contract.
